html:
"Proto-Slavs" is the map's label, for 700, for the early Slavs, the speakers of Slavic dialects who spread across central and eastern Europe from the 500s to the 900s. On the map they fill a vast area from the Elbe to the Dnieper.

They first appear in Byzantine writers of the 500s such as Procopius and Jordanes, who called them Sclaveni and Antes. Where they came from is still argued; most scholars place their homeland somewhere in eastern Europe, near today's Ukraine and Belarus.

They lived in small farming villages of sunken huts, grew millet and wheat, and worshipped gods such as Perun. They had no kings at first. Many lived for a time under the Avars. Their first states were the union of Samo, then Great Moravia, the Bulgarian state, Kievan Rus' and Poland. Over time they split into West, East and South Slavs.
